title: Eggs Benedict Hall Style
subtitle: Poached eggs, Canadian bacon, and hollandaise on toasted English muffins.
description: Adapted from classic New York brunch tradition for a firehall breakfast line: split English muffins toasted crisp, topped with warmed Canadian bacon, poached eggs, and a stable blender hollandaise. Portions cleanly for eight with a two-pan poaching setup.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Eggs Benedict Hall Style in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Bacon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Make hollandaise
steps.instruction: Blend yolks, lemon juice, mustard, and a pinch of salt 30 seconds. With blender running on medium, slowly stream in hot melted butter until thick and glossy. Hold in a thermos or over a warm water bath—not direct heat. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Toast muffins and warm bacon
steps.instruction: Split and toast English muffins at 350°F until edges are crisp, about 6 minutes. Warm Canadian bacon in a dry skillet over medium until lightly browned at the edges; hold covered on a warm tray. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Set poaching water
steps.instruction: Bring two wide pots of water to a gentle simmer with a tablespoon of vinegar each—the surface should barely ripple, not roll. Crack each egg into a small cup before sliding into the water. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale.

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.instruction: Slide eggs into simmering water one at a time. Poach 3–4 minutes until whites are fully set (165°F) and yolks remain runny. Lift with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and trim ragged edges for clean plates. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Eggs Benedict Hall Style onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Assemble and sauce
steps.instruction: Place two muffin halves per plate, top each with bacon and a poached egg. Spoon hollandaise generously over each egg, finish with chives and lemon zest, and serve within 2 minutes while yolks are still liquid. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Make hollandaise first and hold warm—never reheat over direct flame or it will break.
Run two poaching pots in parallel so eight eggs finish within the same 4-minute window.
Toast muffins in batches right before poaching starts; cold muffins kill the dish on the plate.
cleanupNotes: Rinse poaching pots immediately with cold water so egg whites do not cook onto the sides.
Wash blender and whisk while hollandaise is still warm—set butter is miserable to scrub cold.
leftovers: Hollandaise does not reheat well; make a half batch if crew size is uncertain.
Use leftover Canadian bacon and muffins in a breakfast sandwich bake with scrambled eggs.
